answer: Proposal: A grove Merkle root commits each key to a different salt-keyed, memory-hard 48-GiB replica of a reef survey with ferrous sediment records. In one unpredictable 3-second window auditors request 32 random blocks per key; validators check proofs and forfeit pending pay on missing or false blocks. A farm shares one model and rents RAM, its cheapest move, but cross-linked encoding prevents cheap reconstruction from a shared master. Each extra key needs another 48 GiB resident throughout the epoch, even on leased hardware. If a replica is absent, that key earns zero.
